question.text: A trader writes a call with strike Rs. 500 at premium Rs. 15. At expiry, stock is at Rs. 510. What is the writer's profit/loss?

explanation.text: The Logic: Short Call Profit = Premium - max(S - X, 0). With Premium = 15, S = 510, X = 500: payoff to the buyer = max(510 - 500, 0) = Rs. 10, so writer's P/L = 15 - 10 = Rs. 5 profit. The writer profits as long as spot is below X + P = Rs. 515. The Trap: Loss of Rs. 10 takes only the buyer's payoff without crediting the premium. Loss of Rs. 5 inverts the sign. Profit of Rs. 15 ignores the buyer's payoff and assumes the writer keeps the full premium. Note: Broken comparison after "as long as S" repaired — explanation now states "the writer profits as long as spot is below X + P = Rs. 515."
